{'id': '0', 'translation': 'Chief Executive John Lee today attended the Legislative Council\'s first "exchange session" and met the media afterwards with Legislative Council President Starry Lee. Regarding the long-term housing arrangements for Wang Fuk Court, Lee said 53% of owners have signed sale and purchase agreements and urged residents to "decide as soon as possible." On the early retirement of Judge Jonathan Man concerning alleged judicial plagiarism, he said he respects the appropriate measures taken by the Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal to maintain public confidence in the independent and professional fulfilment of judicial duties. Regarding the vacancy left by Wong Kam-fai\'s resignation following a drink-driving charge, Lee pointed out that three important elections will be held in the next 18 months, and priority should be given to these three elections in terms of timing, workload, and relative necessity.'}

{'id': '1', 'translation': 'Chief Executive John Lee attended the Legislative Council\'s "exchange session" today and responded to media questions afterwards.'}

{'id': '2', 'translation': '53% of owners signed sale and purchase agreements; nearly 91% signed letters of intent for acquisition'}

{'id': '3', 'translation': 'When asked about the acquisition of Wang Fuk Court and whether he understood the reasons why some residents had not signed consent forms, Lee said the matter had been handled with "compassion, reason, and law" from the very beginning. He reiterated that regarding long-term housing arrangements, the government is acquiring property titles at a price of HK$8,000 to HK$10,500 per square foot and undertaking various risks, including the uncertainty of insurance compensation and possible legal proceedings.'}

{'id': '4', 'translation': 'He said that as of yesterday, 90.8% of owners had signed letters of intent to accept the acquisition proposal, 53% had signed sale and purchase agreements, and some owners had already completed the property title transfer. He described the process as smooth and urged everyone to "decide as soon as possible." He pointed out that the decision must be made by each household based on their own circumstances, but in terms of acquisition price, risk-bearing, and other support, "we hope to let the relevant households make their decisions as soon as possible so that everyone can return to normal life at an early date." He also mentioned that flats would soon be open for residents to choose: "Seize this opportunity early — you will have the chance to pick your ideal long-term residence."'}

{'id': '5', 'translation': 'Lee reiterated that the government had recently improved the rent allowance arrangements, and the Legislative Council had approved the HK$1 billion funding application for the acquisition of Wang Fuk Court. He said the government would continue its explanatory work, and residents with questions or demands could approach the explanation team or a dedicated social work team, and the authorities would handle matters flexibly and pragmatically based on actual circumstances.'}

{'id': '6', 'translation': 'When asked about the long-term housing arrangements for Wang Fuk Court, Lee said 53% of owners had signed sale and purchase agreements, some owners had completed the property title transfer, and he described the process as smooth.'}

{'id': '7', 'translation': "Responding to Jonathan Man's early retirement over plagiarism: respects the Chief Justice's appropriate measures"}

{'id': '8', 'translation': 'High Court Court of First Instance Judge Jonathan Man was accused of plagiarising on multiple occasions and was required by Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal Andrew Cheung yesterday to take early retirement. When asked whether this could restore public confidence, Lee said that society has high expectations and professional requirements for judges, and the judiciary has always operated and been managed independently. He said he respects the appropriate measures taken by the Chief Justice to maintain public confidence in the independent and professional fulfilment of judicial duties, and is confident that judges and judicial officers at all levels will uphold the judicial oath and perform their duties loyally, independently, and professionally.'}

{'id': '9', 'translation': 'High Court Judge Jonathan Man, who was involved in alleged judicial plagiarism, has been required to take early retirement. The Chief Executive responded today, saying he respects the appropriate measures taken by the Chief Justice to maintain public confidence. (File photo)'}

{'id': '10', 'translation': "Separately, University of Hong Kong (HKU) President Zhang Xiang, who was previously caught up in a governance controversy, announced yesterday that he will step down in 2028 after completing two terms totalling ten years. When asked how he would evaluate Zhang Xiang's performance and whether he would require HKU to include terms on strengthening communication with the Council when recruiting a new president, Lee said Zhang Xiang is a scientist who loves science and is eager to return to the laboratory to solve scientific problems and contribute to society. He thanked Zhang Xiang for notifying the Council of his decision in advance, giving the university ample time to recruit a new president."}

{'id': '11', 'translation': "Lee also thanked Zhang Xiang for his past and future contributions to HKU during his tenure as president, as well as his diligent work for the university. He pointed out that the president's recruitment is the responsibility of the Council, and said the university has a sound president recruitment mechanism. He has full confidence in the Council's handling of this matter and believes it can ensure that the new president will lead HKU to continue to develop and progress."}

{'id': '12', 'translation': "HKU President Zhang Xiang announced yesterday that he will step down in 2028. Lee thanked him for his contributions to HKU and expressed full confidence in the Council's recruitment work. (File photo)"}

{'id': '13', 'translation': "No by-election after Wong Kam-fai's resignation: priority given to three elections"}

{'id': '14', 'translation': 'Legislative Council member Wong Kam-fai was arrested on suspicion of drink-driving at the end of last month and resigned earlier this month, with public attention on whether a by-election would be held. Secretary for Constitutional and Mainland Affairs Alice Mak had previously indicated that the timing was rather tight. When asked again today about the by-election, Lee pointed out that three important elections will be held in the next 18 months: the Election Committee election in November this year, the Chief Executive election in March next year, and the District Council election by the end of next year. He said that for any election, the Electoral Affairs Commission (EAC) will comprehensively consider factors such as manpower resources, venue arrangements, polling station set-up, as well as the procurement and transportation of election materials, and must assess the overall work arrangements and relative necessity of each election based on actual circumstances.'}

{'id': '15', 'translation': 'Lee added that after the Election Committee election is completed in November this year, the committee will be sworn in on February 1 next year to perform the functions of the relevant elections. He believed that, "compared with a by-election for a single vacancy in the Legislative Council, the three elections should be given priority in terms of timing, workload, and relative necessity."'}

{'id': '16', 'translation': "After Wong Kam-fai's resignation due to a drink-driving charge, there was public concern about whether a by-election would be held for the vacancy. Lee said priority should be given to the three upcoming elections, while Legislative Council President Starry Lee said she respects the assessment of the Chief Executive and the EAC."}

{'id': '17', 'translation': 'When asked whether the reduced manpower in the Council would affect its work and whether she had communicated with Xia Baolong, Starry Lee said she understood and respected the assessment of the Chief Executive and the EAC. As an important working partner of the government, the Legislative Council will fully support a series of important tasks including the first five-year plan and the Policy Address. She continued that although the Council has undergone changes, with only 89 members remaining, "I believe every member understands that, facing the new situation brought about by this sudden change, we need to rise to the challenge, support each other, and share the workload." She said all members will go all out, and with 89 people working together, the Council will be able to perform its functions as always.'}

{'id': '18', 'translation': 'No response on whether the new Huanggang Port can open before October 1'}

{'id': '19', 'translation': "The legislative proposals for the Hong Kong Port area of the new Huanggang Port were previously passed by the Legislative Council, and together with the relevant subsidiary legislation, will take effect on July 31. However, the authorities have not yet announced the official opening date. When asked whether the port could officially open before October 1, Lee did not respond directly, only saying that he understood the public's strong anticipation for the port. He pointed out that after the Hong Kong Port area is set up on July 31, the governments of Hong Kong and Shenzhen will conduct operational tests on the port, including systems, equipment, and traffic stress tests. He emphasised that the installation of equipment and facilities, operational tests, and exercises are being推进 at full speed, and it is hoped that they will be completed as soon as possible for public use. Any decision will be announced."}
